note: W7 (OKNA §5.3, §6.3): gestures of the window system as data. Every entry is a preset and the lists are open examples: a target (chain icon, title bar) → for a gesture (tap, long_press, double_tap) the operation. Times in ms.

icon.drag_start_note: R101 D6: how a drag of a desktop icon begins - a word, or {<device class>: word}; known: move (the pointer moves past drag_threshold_px; the icon takes the touch, so a finger on it cannot scroll the desktop), long_press (hold long_press_ms still, then move; a plain swipe scrolls - the phone preset, so a desktop with many icons still scrolls), handle (only a grip ⠿ on the icon drags; the rest scrolls). An unknown word works as move and says so (drag_start_unknown). With long_press, a hold released in place is the long_press gesture (the menu).

chain_cycle_note: The order a tap on the chain walks the binding of a parameter (§5.3: the order is an example). `linked` takes the first other window of the same kind that follows the parameter, dependency same; with none, the step is skipped.
focus_order_note: §6.4: the order of windows for Tab/the switcher keys: the dock tree in reading order (a before b), floating ones by z rising, then the shelf. Any order of these words.
touch_target_px_note: §6.4: the minimum size of the title-bar buttons and grips (CSS px); smaller works.
